definitions: To release an accused person as a result of payment of a sum of money.
To scoop water out of a boat or container.
To abandon a project or situation, often suddenly.
To jump out of an aircraft using a parachute.
examples: The judge agreed to bail the defendant.
We had to bail the water out of the leaking dinghy.
He decided to bail on the meeting at the last minute.
The pilot was forced to bail out over the sea.
